column1: arrogance§There is an arrogance in assuming the reader will look it up.§认定读者自己会去查，这本身就是一种**傲慢**。
arrogant§It would be arrogant to publish without checking the earlier work.§不核对前人的工作就发表未免**傲慢**。
articulate§He could not articulate what was wrong with the design.§他**说不清**这个设计到底哪里不对。
articulation§The articulation between the two beams was the weak point.§两根梁之间的**接合**处是薄弱环节。
artifice§There is no artifice in her prose, which is itself an art.§她的文字**毫无雕饰**，而这本身就是一种艺术。
artistic§Artistic licence does not extend to the dates.§**艺术**加工不适用于日期。
artistry§The artistry lies in what he left out.§他的**艺术功力**在于他省略掉的部分。
ascertain§Ascertain the depth before you anchor.§下锚之前先**探明**水深。
ascetic§The room was ascetic to the point of discomfort.§这个房间**简朴**到令人不适。
asceticism§Her asceticism about deadlines made her unpopular and reliable.§她在截止期限上的**苛己**让她不受欢迎，却很可靠。
aspersion§I cast no aspersion on his motives, only on his arithmetic.§我不**质疑**他的动机，只质疑他的算术。
assault§An assault on the record book, not the mountain, was the point.§目标是**冲击**纪录，而不是征服那座山。
assiduous§Assiduous cleaning revealed a signature under the varnish.§**细致的清理**在清漆下显出了一个签名。
assimilation§Assimilation of the refugees took two generations, not two years.§难民的**融入**用了两代人，而不是两年。
assure§She assured herself that the door was locked and left.§她**确认**了门已锁好才离开。
astute§It was an astute purchase, made a month before the rezoning.§这是一次**精明**的购入，就在改区划前一个月。
attenuate§Time attenuates outrage; documents do not.§时间会**削弱**愤怒，文件不会。
attribution§Quotation without attribution is the one rule nobody may break.§引用不**注明出处**，是唯一谁都不能破的规矩。
atypical§The specimen is atypical and therefore worth keeping.§这个标本**非典型**，因此值得保留。
audacious§The most audacious thing in the book is its first sentence.§这本书里最**大胆的**是它的第一句话。
augment§Overtime augmented the wage but wrecked the schedule.§加班**增加**了工资，却毁了作息。
aural§Her memory is aural: she remembers voices, never faces.§她的记忆是**听觉**型的：只记得声音，从不记得面孔。
auspicious§Not an auspicious start: the projector failed in the first minute.§开头并不**吉利**：投影仪第一分钟就坏了。
austere§An austere budget produced an unusually good year.§一份**紧缩**的预算造就了异常好的一年。
austerity§The austerity of the design is a decision, not a shortage.§这个设计的**简朴**是一种选择，而不是短缺所致。
authenticate§Only two people alive can authenticate that seal.§在世的人中只有两位能**鉴定**那枚印章。
authoritarian§An authoritarian classroom produces quiet, not learning.§**专断**的课堂带来的是安静，而不是学习。
autocrat§A benevolent autocrat is still an autocrat.§仁慈的**独裁者**仍然是独裁者。
autocratic§His autocratic habits survived the arrival of a board.§董事会成立后，他**专制的**习惯依然没变。
autonomy§Departments were given autonomy and then given a template.§各部门先被赋予**自主权**，接着又被发了模板。
avant-garde§Every avant-garde becomes an academy if it lasts long enough.§任何**先锋派**只要存在得够久，都会变成学院派。
avarice§Avarice is patient, which is what makes it dangerous.§**贪婪**是有耐心的，这正是它危险之处。
averse§He is not averse to being wrong in public.§他并不**排斥**当众出错。
aversion§Her aversion to the telephone made her an excellent correspondent.§她对电话的**厌恶**让她成了极好的书信作者。
avert§She averted her eyes from the photograph on the wall.§她把目光从墙上的照片**移开**。
avid§An avid collector will pay for the gap in a series.§**热切**的收藏家愿意为一套里缺的那一件出高价。
avocation§What began as an avocation supported him for thirty years.§起初只是**副业**的事，养活了他三十年。
avoidance§Tax avoidance is legal; the argument is about whether it should be.§**避税**是合法的，争论在于它是否应当合法。
avuncular§An avuncular tone can be as condescending as a stern one.§**长辈式**的语气可能和严厉的语气一样居高临下。
awaken§He awakened to the smell of smoke and no alarm.§他被烟味**惊醒**，警报却没响。
backfire§The engine backfired twice and then ran perfectly.§发动机**回火**了两次，随后运转得非常好。
backlash§The backlash came from the group the change was meant to help.§**反弹**恰恰来自这项改动本想帮助的那群人。
ballad§Ballads travel further than treaties do.§**歌谣**比条约传播得更远。
banal§Nothing is more banal than a warning nobody reads.§没有什么比一条无人阅读的警告更**陈腐**。
banality§Behind the banality of the phrasing was a genuine threat.§**平庸**的措辞背后是一个真实的威胁。
bane§Paperwork was the bane of a job he otherwise loved.§文书工作是他原本热爱的这份工作里的**祸根**。
baneful§A baneful rumor spread faster than the correction.§**有害**的谣言传得比更正快。
bankrupt§The argument is intellectually bankrupt and rhetorically effective.§这个论证在思想上**一无所有**，在修辞上却很有效。
banter§Banter is a poor substitute for an actual answer.§**插科打诨**代替不了一个真正的答案。
baroque§The accounting was baroque enough to hide anything.§这套账目**繁复**到足以藏下任何东西。
barrage§An artillery barrage preceded the crossing by two hours.§渡河前两小时进行了**炮火覆盖**。
barter§Before there were coins here, everything moved by barter.§这里出现钱币之前，一切都靠**以物易物**。
beautify§Beautifying the entrance did nothing for the queue inside.§**美化**入口对里面的排队毫无帮助。
bedazzle§Do not let a good title bedazzle you into skipping the method.§别让一个好标题**晃花了眼**，跳过方法部分。
beguile§The brochure beguiled hundreds into a very cold sea.§宣传册**诱使**数百人下了极冷的海。
behavior§Behavior in the wild differs sharply from behavior in a tank.§野外的**行为**与水箱中的行为差别很大。
belated§Belated recognition arrived with a plaque and no pension.§**迟来的**认可只带来一块铜牌，没有养老金。
belie§The quiet street belies what happens here on a Saturday.§这条安静的街道**掩盖**了周六这里的景象。
belittle§He belittled his own contribution until nobody remembered it.§他一再**贬低**自己的贡献，直到没人记得。
bellicose§A bellicose headline sold papers and cost lives.§**好战的**标题卖了报纸，也害了性命。
belligerence§Belligerence in a negotiation usually means the case is weak.§谈判中的**好斗**通常意味着理据薄弱。
benefactor§The benefactor asked only that the reading room stay open late.§这位**捐助者**只要求阅览室开放到很晚。
beneficial§A short delay proved beneficial to everyone but the printer.§短暂的推迟对除印厂之外的所有人都**有益**。
beneficiary§The chief beneficiary of the reform was the department that opposed it.§这项改革最大的**受益者**是反对它的那个部门。
benefit§The benefit of the doubt is not the same as agreement.§**姑且相信**并不等于同意。
benevolent§A benevolent silence is still a silence.§**善意**的沉默仍然是沉默。
benign§A benign climate hides how thin the soil actually is.§**温和**的气候掩盖了土壤实际有多薄。
